subject: DPA: retention window exception & subprocessor clarification needed
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@acme-analytics.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@acme-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions: retention windows & subprocessors

Hi Grace,

Thanks for sending over the DPA draft. Our legal team has two substantive asks before we can proceed:

1) Data retention window: We're requesting a 540-day retention window for aggregated telemetry derived from customer logs (some of our compliance is still on that cadence). Your current DPA has a 365-day default retention for telemetry. Is Redwood able to make an exception for telemetry buckets tied to paid accounts?

2) Subprocessors: we need a complete, up-to-date list of subprocessors (including cloud marketplaces and managed logging providers) and a commitment to notify Acme prior to onboarding any new subprocessors with 30 days' notice. Can you provide the inventory and acceptance of a 30-day notification clause?

I've attached our internal summary for context. We can be flexible on some language but need Product & Security signoff that the retention exception and the notification commitment are feasible operationally.

Best,
Maya
Legal Counsel, Acme Analytics

Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_request.pdf (pdf)

Team — forwarding Acme's asks below. Can Product and Security confirm operational impact and whether we can accept these as a spot exception? Quick notes:

- Retention: Acme wants 540 days for telemetry derived from customer logs tied to their account. Product: is this a config knob we can surface per-tenant? Ops: any cost or perf implications to keeping KV/prefix caches or telemetry for 1.5 years?
- Subprocessors: they want a full inventory + 30-day notice before onboarding. Security: we currently publish a subprocessor list and do 60-day notice for major infra changes; is 30 days OK, and can Legal route notifications?

If we can, I'd like to prep a redline to the DPA and push back a timeline of 3 business days for them to review.

—Grace
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA questions: retention windows & subprocessors

Grace — quick take from SecOps:

- Subprocessor inventory: we can produce a snapshot (cloud infra providers, managed logging, monitoring, SSO, analytics partners) as of today. The file will need weekly updates until signing; attaching the latest export.
- Notification window: 30 days is acceptable for infra-level subprocessors we control. For third-party marketplace-supplied connectors, notice timing varies (some are vendor-managed). We should avoid blanket language that promises notification for vendor-managed marketplace changes. Suggest language: "Redwood will provide at least 30 days' notice prior to onboarding or materially changing subprocessors under Redwood's direct control; marketplace-delivered components will be listed and updated but may be subject to vendor timelines."

- Retention window: Product/Storage needs to chime in. Operationally we can keep telemetry for 540 days, but cost and egress impact must be assessed on their plan. Also need to confirm whether "telemetry derived from customer logs" is equivalently identifiable per-account or if it requires cross-account aggregation that complicates per-tenant retention.

I'll flag two security items we want in the redline: (1) limit of subprocessor access to production data (least privilege clause), and (2) notification cadence plus a rolling public subprocessor page.

—Laura
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_20260829.pdf (pdf)

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA questions: retention windows & subprocessors

Thanks — product notes:

- Retention: we can expose a per-tenant telemetry retention setting tied to billing tier (standard = 365d, enterprise = 540d) and enforce via lifecycle policies on the telemetry index/archival buckets. Implementation effort: ~3 sprints (2 infra, 1 infra-tests + docs). For an exception in a contract effective immediately, we can accept as a one-off operational flag (manual config) but we'd like to include a revision milestone: finalize an automated per-tenant config by Q4 and roll into the platform SLA.

- Cost: estimate +8–12% monthly cost for storage and query ops for the tenant if telemetry is retained at 540d vs 365d. If Acme is on a committed capacity plan, we can offset with a billing credit.

- Subprocessors: product supports generating a stable inventory export and adding a webhook-based notification for legal to consume. Requires small API endpoint and an internal runbook. ETA: 2 weeks for a first-pass endpoint.

Recommendation: Legal and CS offer an interim exception: (a) consent to 540d for Acme as an enterprise provision; (b) provide current snapshot of subprocessors and accept our proposed 30-day-notice-for-direct-subprocessors language. We should document implementation milestones in the DPA redline (manual flag now, automated per-tenant setting by Q4).

—Dev
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Maya Patel <maya@acme-analytics.com>, contracts@acme-analytics.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions: retention windows & subprocessors

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear asks and context. Quick summary and proposed steps from Redwood:

1) Retention window: We can accept a 540-day telemetry retention for Acme as an enterprise-specific exception. Operationally this will be deployed as a manual config flag today; Product commits to ship an automated per-tenant retention setting (standard/enterprise tiers) by Q4 2026. If acceptable, we'll add a redline clause that states: "Redwood will retain telemetry derived from Customer logs for up to 540 days for covered Acme accounts, implemented as a contractual exception; Redwood will provide an automated per-tenant retention control by 2026-12-15." We are open to a one-time billing credit to offset incremental storage costs — details to be agreed by Finance if Acme moves forward.

2) Subprocessors & notice: Attached is our current subprocessor inventory snapshot. Redwood agrees to provide at least 30 days' notice prior to onboarding subprocessors that Redwood directly engages and controls. We cannot promise control over third-party marketplace-managed connectors; language below clarifies that marketplace-delivered components may be subject to external vendor timelines. Security will include least-privilege limits in the redline.

Next steps: I've attached a redline of the DPA with the proposed exception language and a footnote with implementation milestones. Please review and let us know if Acme can accept the manual-exception + Q4 automation milestone. If yes, Legal and Product can sign off and we'll route the final to DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call this week if you prefer.

Best,
Grace
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
